testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces called?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice may look wet. Be very careful when it is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Which sign shows that water is standing on the road?

options.text: Portions of the pavement that are dry

questions.explanation: Standing water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Tire splashes, clear reflections, or raindrops on the road can show where water is collecting.

questions.question: What endorsement test do you need to transport hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: Why should you cover your cargo?

options.text: To protect the cargo from thieves.
To protect the cargo from weather.
To prevent other drivers from looking at what is being transported.
To keep the cargo a secret.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from weather.
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect it from weather and to keep cargo from spilling onto other drivers or the road.

questions.question: When should you turn off your turn signal?
questions.explanation: Keep your turn signal on the whole time you are turning. Turn it off only after you finish the turn.

questions.question: What do the air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold only enough air for one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for the brakes to be used several times if the compressor stops working.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to be used several times if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air for braking. They store enough air to let you brake several times even if the compressor fails.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: When passing, assume the other driver does not see you. This keeps you safe.

questions.question: What can rough acceleration do?

options.text: Is common if a vehicle is warmed up.
Is encouraged to improve gas mileage.

questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can harm your vehicle's engine and other parts.

questions.question: What causes distracted driving?

options.text: Can only be caused by physical distractions.
Can only be caused by mental distractions.
Can be caused by physical and/or mental distractions.
Can only be caused by cell phone use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be caused by physical and/or mental distractions.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for objects), mental (talking with passengers), or both (holding a phone to text).

questions.question: How many tie-downs must secure cargo at minimum?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, always use at least two tie-downs, no matter how small the cargo is.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Get a full night of sleep before driving.
Schedule trips during times when you normally sleep.

questions.correctAnswerText: Schedule trips during times when you normally sleep.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. To prevent drowsiness, get enough sleep before driving, have a passenger to share driving duties, schedule trips when you are normally awake, and avoid drowsy medications.

questions.question: Texting while driving is dangerous because:

options.text: It creates both mental and physical distractions.
A message may upset the driver.
Texts may be more interesting than driving.
Texting is less efficient than calling.

questions.correctAnswerText: It creates both mental and physical distractions.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it distracts you mentally and physically.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Okay if the weather is clear.
Allowed if it is for work.

questions.explanation: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and finish the trip.

questions.explanation: The only way to deal with drowsiness is to stop and sleep. Caffeine and other drugs may help you stay awake temporarily, but you will become even more tired when they wear off.

questions.question: Which is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial trucks must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: To secure 30 feet of cargo on a flatbed trailer, use at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo must have a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, how do you follow the trailer's turn?

options.text: Do nothing. The vehicle will naturally follow the trailer.
Change the direction of the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel harder in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change the direction of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel opposite to the desired direction. Once the trailer turns, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: After starting a trip with cargo, when should you inspect it?

options.text: You do not need to inspect the cargo.
Only if it is making noise.
Only if there is an obvious problem.
After 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: After 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before the trip starts, after the first 50 miles, and then every 3 hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: A five-foot item on a flatbed trailer must be secured by at least:
questions.explanation: Use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo needs at least two tie-downs, no matter how small.

questions.question: Where should a helper stand when you back up?

options.text: In front of the passenger side.
In front of the driver side.
On the side of the truck.
Near the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your helper should stand near the back of the truck where you can see them. Agree on hand signals before backing up, including a signal to stop.

questions.question: Where should you place the heaviest cargo when loading a trailer?

options.text: On top of the lighter cargo.
At the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Heavy cargo should go underneath lighter cargo. This prevents the vehicle from being top-heavy, which can cause rollovers.

questions.question: If you see a large box in your lane ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Don't worry because another vehicle will hit it first.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful. Even light objects like cardboard boxes can contain hard or heavy items that damage your vehicle.

questions.question: What maneuvers might be on a basic vehicle control skills test?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test can include straight line backing, offset back parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When you need to turn quickly to avoid an object, what should you do?

options.text: Turn more than needed to clear the object.
Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
questions.explanation: Turn only enough to clear the object. Do not brake while turning.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) is not working properly.

questions.question: What should you NOT do at a railroad crossing during a driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Never stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: When backing up, what is the best practice?

options.text: Use only the passenger's side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger's side whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Back up slowly and use both side mirrors. Have a helper watch your blind spots if possible. Agree on a signal to stop.

questions.question: What is another name for a front-end header board?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called headache racks. They protect the driver if cargo moves during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy manner without regard for others
Driving with some care for other motorists' safety

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy manner without regard for others
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy way without care for the rights or safety of others.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of deaths and injuries in work zones. Drive carefully when near road workers.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually cannot see or understand what is happening.
Is usually aware of what is happening around them.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually cannot see or understand what is happening.
questions.explanation: A distracted driver may not see hazards, may make poor decisions, and may react badly. Stay away from distracted drivers when you can.

questions.question: When a vehicle is started, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, the coolant temperature should gradually increase to the normal operating level.

questions.question: A CMV driver with any detectable alcohol but below the legal limit will:

options.text: Result in an out-of-service order for two hours.
Result in an out-of-service order for 10 hours.
Result in an out-of-service order for 24 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Result in an out-of-service order for 24 hours.
questions.explanation: If you have any detectable alcohol in your system while driving a CMV, even if below the legal limit of 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for 24 hours. Never drive a vehicle under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving:

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
The engine should be turned off.
The check can be done from inside the vehicle.
The check can be done by looking at a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: To check your lights, set the parking brake, turn off the engine, and remove the key. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out and check that all lights are working.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles get into the lane you wish to occupy.
Move slowly, in case another vehicle is in the lane you wish to occupy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly, in case another vehicle is in the lane you wish to occupy.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to get out of your way or honk to warn you. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a cause for concern since it is stopped.
Is only a concern if passengers are exiting the bus.
Is always a concern, whether or not passengers are visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether or not passengers are visible.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when driving near a stopped bus. Passengers may be near it, and the bus can block your view or theirs.

questions.question: Engine belts should:
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts for tightness and wear. Each belt should have the right amount of give for your vehicle.

questions.question: When loading cargo, weight should be placed:

options.text: As close to the cab as possible.

questions.explanation: Keep cargo weight as low as possible to reduce the risk of the vehicle tipping over.

questions.question: If you don't pass the air brakes endorsement test:

options.text: You won't be permitted to drive a vehicle with air brakes.
Your CDL will include an air brake endorsement marked with an asterisk.

questions.correctAnswerText: You won't be permitted to drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: If you don't take or pass the air brakes test, you cannot drive vehicles with air brakes.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, the driver should:

options.text: Obtain special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to get them to move from the lane closest to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obtain special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Special permits are required for loads that are over-length, over-width, or overweight. You must follow all special driving rules.

questions.question: Retreaded tires:

options.text: Can be used on the front axle of a school bus.
Can be used on the rear axles of a school bus.
Cannot be used on a school bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used on the rear axles of a school bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus. They can only be used on the rear axles.

questions.question: When taking a driving test:

options.text: You must provide the same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
You can provide any type of vehicle, even if it is different from the vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
The testing station will provide the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must provide the same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
questions.explanation: You must take the skills test in the same type of vehicle you plan to drive. You are responsible for providing the test vehicle.

questions.question: If you drive in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license should you choose?
questions.explanation: If you drive in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, you must choose a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: When approaching a construction worker near the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully through work zones. Reduce your speed when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Speed up and slow down often.
Change your driving to match the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your driving to match the weather.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, adjust your speed to match conditions. Your vehicle will take longer to stop, so increase your distance from other vehicles. Do not change speeds often.

questions.question: Bridges usually freeze:

options.text: Only when temperatures drop well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Be extra careful on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: How is water and compressor oil removed from an air storage tank?

options.text: The water and oil are siphoned out.
Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil.
The water and oil are removed automatically when brakes are used.
A sponge is used to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil.
questions.explanation: Water and compressor oil are removed through a drain valve. These must be drained from the tank every day. If not removed, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while driving a placarded vehicle, you should always:

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks in a placarded vehicle, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while your vehicle is crossing the tracks.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system is very low on pressure:

options.text: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable change.
Lights on the outside of the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop your vehicle safely and get the system repaired.

questions.question: What should you do if your braking system cannot build up pressure?

options.text: Press the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.explanation: If your brakes will not build up pressure to slow or stop your vehicle, try shifting to a lower gear, pumping the brakes, and using the emergency brake.
